# A second invoice for the same customer, settled by the credit the first one
# parked — named the short way, with `txn_guid:` and nothing else.
#
# The transaction it names is the 200.00 USD deposit already divided by
# INV-USD-RETARGET: 100.00 settled that invoice, and 100.00 stayed as the
# customer's credit, in a lot of its own with a cost basis on it. This invoice
# is for exactly that 100.00, so the whole of the credit split moves into its
# lot.
#
# What the file does not say is that the money comes out of credit — a
# `from_credit:` block would, and this is the same physical move reached the
# short way. The import has to work that out from where the split is sitting,
# because the accounting differs: currency that has been spent carries no
# basis, and a split left holding one has the book offering USD it no longer
# has.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.

invoice "INV-USD-SECOND"
	customer_id: "C-US"
	currency: USD
	date_opened: 2026-03-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-03-01
		description: "More consulting"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-03-01
		due: 2026-04-01
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
		memo: "Invoice INV-USD-SECOND"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-03-01
		amount: 100
		bank_account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
		txn_guid: "TXN_GUID"
		memo: "Settled from the credit on account"
